newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open near unch before jobless data.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open near unch before jobless data.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices opened unchanged to slightly lower on Thursday in front of the government's weekly report on new jobless claims.
Economists forecast that the Labor Department will report 336,000 new claims for state unemployment insurance in the week ended October 19, down from 340,000 a week earlier.

But they said the claims data could be distorted because the Columbus Day holiday fell during the survey week and also because of the potential impact of the now-concluded Canadian autoworkers strike against General Motors.
While the strike occurred in Canada, it eventually led to temporary layoffs of about 19,000 GM workers in the U.S.
But David Sloan, economist at I.D.E.A., said most of that strike impact would be felt in next week's data.

"The Canadian GM strike boosted the number of GM layoffs in the U.S. last week, which will produce a few thousand additional claims, but poor seasonal factors will be at work as well," said Greg Jones, economist at MMS International. "The bottom line is that claims, despite their weekly volatility, are not indicating any chnage in underlying labor market conditions over the past month."
Besides the jobless claims data, "there's not a great deal on the calendar," said Sloan.
Sloan characterized the market as "a little vulnerable" as it digests recent supply.
The Treasury sold $12.5 billion in five-year notes on Wednesday and $18.25 billion in two-year notes on Tuesday.
Both auctions were well bid. The market retreated after the two-year auction but rallied after the five-year sale.
The steady to unchanged open occurred after a fairly steady session overnight, said Kim Rupert, economist at MMS International.
Minutes before the jobless claims data, prices in the middle and long sector of the maturity range eased.
The 6-3/4 percent 30-year bond was down 5/32 to 98-26/32.
The 6-1/2 percent ten-year note was down 1/32 to 99-19/32, yielding 6.56 percent.
Two-year notes were down 1/32 to 99-28/32, yielding 5.94 percent. Five-year notes were down 3/32 to 99-25/32, yielding 6.30 percent.
Three-month bill rates were down one basis point to 4.98 percent. -- North American Treasury Desk, 212-859-1679
